prerequisites: Knowledge of Technical Drawing is required.
Having completed the subject Graphic Expression and Computer-Aided Drawing is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies typically demonstrated by developing and defending arguments and solving problems within their area of study.

Ability to draft, sign, and develop projects in the field of industrial engineering related to the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly, or exploitation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical and electronic installations.
Ability to manage the activities subject to the engineering projects described in competence CG01.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Knowledge and abilities for the creation and interpretation of plans and diagrams in the industrial field.
Ability to apply knowledge in practice.
Ability to communicate with non-experts in the field.
Aptitude for oral and written communication in the native language.
Ability for autonomous and deep learning.
Ability to fluently use IT at a user level.
Ability to work in a multidisciplinary team.
Ability to graphically perceive and represent parts, machine elements, mechanisms, and product structures.
Ability to graphically perceive and represent different types of installations, in different representation systems.

syllabus_topics: Mechanical Drawing: Surface qualities and standard numbers
Fundamentals of Electrical Drawing: Electrical diagrams
Fundamentals of Electrical Drawing: Graphic symbols
Fundamentals of Electrical Drawing: Classification of electrical diagrams by representation types
Fundamentals of Electrical Drawing: Study, drawing, and creation of electrical diagrams
Fundamentals of Electrical Drawing: Drawings and diagrams in buildings
teaching_methods: Autonomous student work (self-study of theory and practical exercises)
assessment_rules: The final grade is determined by a theoretical exam (50%), a practical exam (40%), and practical exercises (10%). The theoretical exam evaluates acquired knowledge through short questions. The practical exam assesses the student's ability to produce technical documentation by hand. Practical exercises during the semester develop technical documentation skills. Attendance and performance during practical sessions will be considered in the overall evaluation.
